values.value: Is there a send-frequency policy, and does the suppression infrastructure that enforces it exist in the target tenant yet?

[{"value":1,"label":"No policy and no infrastructure. How often a contact is mailed is whatever the campaign calendar produces."},{"value":2,"label":"A cap policy exists \u2014 in the current platform's settings or on paper \u2014 but nothing is built target-side to enforce it."},{"value":3,"label":"The suppression data extension and its automation are in place target-side, and the cap windows are agreed."}]

capabilities/platforms/sfmc.yaml — infrastructure.frequency_capping names the exact artefacts ("ENT - Email Frequency Suppression" DE, NextEligibleDate field, "ENT - Email Frequency Filter Suppression" automation running hourly against weekly and monthly caps), and gap_patterns traffic_control_loop makes the point this question exists for: in SFMC, capping is INFRASTRUCTURE, not something a journey expresses. reference/ma-migrator-capabilities/platforms/hubspot.yaml — the sending.frequency_capping block, where HubSpot's cap is an account-level setting with a per-email override, i.e. a checkbox the client will assume comes with them. It does not; something has to be built, and this asks whether it has been.
